item.title: Deploying NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard with LiteLLM on AWS
item.description:
Deploying NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard with LiteLLM on AWS

LiteLLM now includes a native built-in Switchyard stage router, allowing developers to route AI model requests through an open source gateway. By using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK), you can deploy this configuration on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.

🧩 How it works

Switchyard acts as a routing plugin that allows an AI agent to choose which model handles each request. The integration functions by sending an OpenAI-compatible request with the model field set to the specific LiteLLM model group. The system operates on Amazon Bedrock using the Converse or ConverseStream API.

⚙️ Key details

  • Routing Strategies: The plugin supports Stage routing (choosing between two candidates) and Random routing (traffic splits via weight for A/B comparisons).
  • Infrastructure: The setup uses an Application Load Balancer, AWS WAF for request filtering, and Amazon Route 53 for hostname resolution.
  • Security: AWS Secrets Manager handles gateway keys, and the task security group limits access strictly to the load balancer.
  • Monitoring: Logs are maintained in Amazon CloudWatch for 30 days, with metrics collected via Container Insights.

🛠 Routing Strategies

Strategy Requirements Function
Stage Exactly two candidates Picks between a capable model and a lower-cost efficient model
Random At least two candidates Picks from configured models using optional weights

Note: Classifier-backed strategies, such as Task and Composite routing, require intermediate model calls that this integration does not support.

#AWS #LiteLLM #NVIDIA #AI #LLM

Source: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Self‑Service LLM Gateway on AWS Bedrock Using LiteLLM
item.description:
Self‑Service LLM Gateway on AWS Bedrock Using LiteLLM

A new self‑service LLM gateway abstracts Amazon Bedrock behind an OpenAI‑compatible API by running LiteLLM on AWS Fargate. The pattern provides a centrally managed access point for coding assistants and other developers.

🔍 Overview

  • An LLM gateway offers a single, centrally managed entry point to foundation models.
  • Developers reach the gateway through a single API key, gaining per‑user cost controls and model performance observability.
  • The post demonstrates the pattern with Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku models.

🧩 How it works

  • Entry point: OpenAI‑compatible client → Amazon Route 53 → Amazon CloudFront → Application Load Balancer (ALB).
  • Authentication: Per‑user API key validated by LiteLLM running on Fargate.
  • State storage: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) holds virtual‑key and spend state; a separate RDS instance stores persistent API‑key metadata and spend tracking.
  • Caching & secrets: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey provides non‑persistent response caching; AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets.
  • Model invocation: LiteLLM invokes Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles using a scoped IAM task role; each model has its own profile managed with AWS CDK.
  • Observability: Amazon CloudWatch captures requests‑per‑minute (RPM) and tokens‑per‑minute (TPM) metrics and triggers quota alarms; Langfuse adds prompt‑level telemetry and latency tracking.
  • Scaling: LiteLLM runs in an AWS Fargate task with target‑tracking auto‑scaling on CPU utilization.
  • Admin portal: A lightweight web portal (integrates with corporate SSO) lets ops engineers set spend policies and developers self‑provision API keys within those limits. The portal also coordinates rate‑limiting across Fargate tasks.
Model Inference Profile Management
Claude Sonnet Managed with AWS CDK
Claude Haiku Managed with AWS CDK

⚙️ Key details

  • OpenAI‑compatible proxy exposed by LiteLLM.
  • Per‑user API keys and spend limits enforce cost control.
  • Per‑model quota isolation via separate inference profiles.
  • Rate‑limiting and non‑persistent caching handled by Valkey.
  • CloudWatch metrics (RPM, TPM) plus Langfuse application‑level insights.
  • Developers can configure tools such as Claude Code, Continue, and Cursor with a single base URL and API key.

🚀 Availability

  • The LiteLLM AI Gateway component is open source and suitable for small pilots (free for up to five users).
  • A license is required for more than five users.
  • LiteLLM Enterprise provides a production‑ready version with SSO, audit logs, delegated admin roles, and support; it also enables the self‑service key issuance described.

💡 Why it matters

  • Centralizes access to multiple foundation models, simplifying integration for development teams.
  • Provides granular cost and usage controls per developer.
  • Combines infrastructure‑level metrics with application‑level observability for easier debugging and performance tuning.

#LLM #AWS #LiteLLM #Bedrock #AIInfrastructure

Source: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM | Amazon Web Services

item.title: LiteLLM Open Source AI Gateway Launches for 100+ LLM Providers
item.description:
LiteLLM Open Source AI Gateway Launches for 100+ LLM Providers

LiteLLM, an open source AI Gateway, has been released, offering a unified interface to call over 100 LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, and more, using the OpenAI format.

🔍 Overview

LiteLLM provides a single, centralized interface to interact with multiple LLM providers, eliminating the need for provider-specific SDKs.

⚙️ Key details

  • Unified API for 100+ LLMs, enabling seamless switching between providers without code changes
  • Drop-in OpenAI compatibility
  • Production-ready gateway with features such as:
    • Virtual keys
    • Spend tracking
    • Guardrails
    • Load balancing
    • Admin dashboard
  • Performance: 8ms P95 latency at 1k requests per second
  • Supports all OpenAI endpoints: /chat/completions, /responses, /embeddings, /images, /audio, /batches, /rerank, /a2a, /messages
  • Rust core with Python SDK

🚀 Availability

  • Deployable as a Python SDK for direct library integration
  • Deployable as an AI Gateway (Proxy Server) for teams or organizations
  • Installation via uv add litellm

#LiteLLM #AIgateway #LLM #OpenAI #PythonSDK #ProxyServer
